title: Law of total probability for finite-range variables

ProbabilityTheory.sum_meas_smul_cond_fib.statement: (Law of total probability.) Let $X:\Omega\to G$ be a measurable random variable with finite range and $\mu$ a measure on $\Omega$. Then $\sum_{x\in \mathrm{range}(X)} \mu(X^{-1}\{x\})\cdot \mu[\,\cdot \mid X^{-1}\{x\}] = \mu$, where $\mu[\,\cdot\mid A]$ denotes the conditional measure on $A$ and the sum runs over the finite range of $X$ (FiniteRange.toFinset $X$).
ProbabilityTheory.sum_meas_smul_cond_fib.sketch: The fibres $X^{-1}\{x\}$, $x$ in the finite range of $X$ (using the Fintype structure on the range), partition $\Omega$, and on each fibre $\mu(X^{-1}\{x\})\,\mu[\cdot\mid X^{-1}\{x\}]$ is the restriction of $\mu$; summing gives $\mu$.
